key_insight: Re-TRAC compresses and organizes entire agent trajectories into structured, recursive state summaries so agents can revisit, branch, and cross-examine past search paths instead of following a single linear trace. This enables global awareness and more efficient, uncertainty-aware exploration in long-horizon LLM-based agents.
problem_solved: Overcomes the limitations of linear ReAct-style agents that cannot easily revisit earlier states, branch into alternative search directions, or maintain global context under long trajectories, which causes redundant exploration and local optima.
method: After each trajectory, generate a structured state summary capturing evidence, uncertainties, key decisions, and outcomes.
Recursively compress trajectories into a hierarchical memory/graph that supports cross-trajectory queries, branching, and selective unrolling.
Use the compressed state representations to guide future planning and uncertainty-aware exploration, enabling revisits and alternative search directions.
impact: Makes LLM-based search agents more scalable and efficient for long-horizon tasks by reducing redundant work, improving global planning, and enabling systematic exploration of alternatives. Practitioners get better performance with fewer tokens and clearer traceability of decisions.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: linear ReAct trace vs recursive compressed-trajectory graph showing branching and revisits
Flowchart: generate trajectory → compress state summary → store in hierarchical memory → query for planning
Bar/line chart: search efficiency or success rate vs trajectory length comparing ReAct and Re-TRAC
Icon set: evidence, uncertainty, branch, and compressed memory to illustrate core components
paper_title: RE-TRAC: REcursive TRAjectory Compression for Deep Search Agents
paper_authors: Jialiang Zhu, Gongrui Zhang, Xiaolong Ma, Lin Xu, Miaosen Zhang
